title: Hard to Start? Friction Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Push a heavy cupboard: nothing, harder, still nothing, then it jerks forward. Diya's steel trunk takes all her strength to start, yet a gentler push keeps it sliding. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we meet the two kinds of friction: static and kinetic.

On a live simulation the push on the trunk grows step by step while static friction matches it, up to its maximum. Then the trunk gives way, friction drops to a smaller, nearly constant kinetic value, and the friction vs push graph shows the classic 45 degree rise, peak and drop to a flat line, with a slow-mo replay of the moment it slips. We build the rule in five small steps, see link by link why starting is harder than sliding, and test it with two pause-and-think questions. Then a worked example, the exam trap about "maximum friction at rest", an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Stuck, stuck, then it slides
0:25 What is friction? Static and kinetic
0:48 The trunk sim: friction vs push, live graph
1:48 The rule, step by step
2:25 Why starting is harder, link by link
2:48 Side by side + pause and think
3:20 Diya lets go + pause and think
3:44 Worked example
4:19 Exam trap
4:41 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:25 Recap and three questions

Next episode: Coefficient of Friction. Put a second trunk on top and friction grows. By how much? One number, mu, tells us.
